messages.author: b548117c8aed3bfb
messages.subject: Units for matern2d latent model
parts:
Hello,
I am fitting a spatial model to a grid using the matern2d model.
Am I correct in assuming that the units for the range are numbers of grid cells? e.g. If I have grid cells that are 600*600 metres, and the mode of the posterior estimate for the range is 10, then that represents a range of 6000 metres?

Here is the full model call:

y <- inla.matrix2vector(ymat)
x <- inla.matrix2vector(xmat)
node <- which(!is.na(y))
dat <- data.frame(x = x, y = y, node = node)

form <- y ~ x + offset(xoffset) +
    f(node, model = "matern2d", nu = 1, nrow = nrow, ncol = ncol,
        hyper = list(range = list(param = c(1,1),
        prior = "loggamma",
        initial = 1),
        prec = list(param = c(1,1))))

m1 <- inla(form, family = 'poisson', data = dat,
    control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE, link = 1), keep = F)

#Plot posterior density for range:
plot(m1$marginals.hyperpar[[2]], type = 'l')

where ymat is the spatial grid (as a matrix) for the response values, xmat is grid for a predictor and node is a vector of positions for where we have observations.

Thanks,
Chris

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Units for matern2d latent model
parts:
Hi

the unit is 1, so a range 10 are 10 units or grid cells.

I would rather use the spde-models instead... which do the same but
more efficiently and more general

H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Units for matern2d latent model
parts:
Hello Chris and Håvard, and thank you for the information provided about this topic. Since I have a model set like the one showed by Chris (count data in a regular grid) would it be possible to understand on which basis the additional parameters (hyper, prior, initial, prec) of the "matern2d" model are defined?

For example, I understood that the range is expressed as units of the grid cell (mine are 10x10 km), but what does it mean specifying:

- range = list(param = c(1,1)
- initial = 1
- prec = list(param = c(1,1))

And what are the reasons behind choosing to set those specific values? Thank you both in advance for your help. It is really appreciated!

Nico

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Units for matern2d latent model
parts:
there is no rational decision behind this, just tried to be sensible. we
have moved away from matern2d to the SPDE models for which the priors
can be justified and motivated through the PC-prior framework. Hence the
matern2d is 'old' and not in use anymore... (hence we will not change
it).

but the unit for matern2d is 1, whatever unit you use. 1 related to the
'range' so the size of one cell, in pratice, is 1/range, about. and you
want/need 1/range to be 'small', like, < 0.25, maybe.
